title: Collect clean email addresses past the nulls

blocks.text: A method reference such as `String::toLowerCase` calls its method on whatever element arrives, so a `null` element throws a `NullPointerException`. The page's fix is to filter with `Objects::nonNull` before the reference that would dereference it.
`User` is a record with a `name` and an `email`. Write `Emails.normalised(List<User> users)`: it returns every user's email, lower-cased, without duplicates, in ascending order.
Try to write the whole pipeline in method references. A list can hold `null` users, a user can have a `null` email, and the same address can be written in different cases.

cases.says: It returns the users' emails lower-cased and sorted.
A null user in the list is skipped, not dereferenced by User::email.
A user whose email is null is skipped, not handed to String::toLowerCase.
Two emails that differ only in case count once, so duplicates are removed after lower-casing.
Two equal addresses that are separate String objects count once; duplicates are found with equals, not identity.

concepts: Method references do not guard against null elements, so nulls are filtered out first with Objects::nonNull.
